panels.title: Successful restic backups (last 48h)
panels.description: Counted from the 'Finished backup at' line restic writes to stdout. BACKUP_CRON runs at 04:00 and 16:00, so a healthy value is 2 or more. Alloy only tails new lines, so this reads 0 until the first backup after it started.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Stacked to total host CPU utilisation. iowait climbing is usually backup, prune or Loki compaction.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: No swap is configured on this host, so exhaustion means an OOM kill rather than paging.

panels.title: Hottest CPU package

targets.expr: max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius * on(host, chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label=~"Package id.*|Tdie|Tctl"})

panels.description: Package temperature, across every host that reports one — the NAS only, today. The bands are set well below the ~100C at which these parts throttle, so orange means look at airflow rather than anything is failing.

panels.title: CPU package temperature

targets.expr: node_hwmon_temp_celsius * on(host, chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label=~"Package id.*|Tdie|Tctl"}

panels.description: One line per host. The package sensor is the whole-die reading and is the one to watch; per-core detail is in the panel alongside.

panels.title: CPU temperature by core

targets.expr: node_hwmon_temp_celsius * on(host, chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label=~"Core .*"}

panels.description: One core running persistently hotter than its siblings points at a pinned single-threaded process rather than a cooling problem — cross-check against CPU by mode in the Host row.

panels.title: Drives failing SMART
panels.description: smartctl's overall-health self-assessment. A drive only fails this after it has already crossed a vendor threshold, so a non-zero value here means replace now, not investigate later. Bad sectors is the tile that moves first.

panels.title: Hottest drive
panels.description: Across spinning disks and NVMe together. The thresholds suit the NVMe drives, which sit around 45C at idle; a 3.5in HDD above 45C is already worth checking the bay's airflow for, well below the orange band.

panels.title: Bad sectors / media errors
panels.description: Reallocated, pending and offline-uncorrectable sectors on the SATA drives, plus NVMe media errors. These counters only ever climb, so zero is the only good value and any movement at all is the earliest warning SMART gives.

panels.title: Drive temperature
panels.description: A steady gap between the two NAS HDDs usually means airflow or bay position rather than a fault; both climbing together tracks NAS load.

panels.title: Drive status

targets.expr: smartctl_device_smart_status * on(host, device) group_left(model_name, serial_number, interface) smartctl_device

sum by (host, device) (smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw",attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable"}) or sum by (host, device) (smartctl_device_media_errors)

panels.description: One row per drive smartctl can see. Health and Bad sectors are the two columns worth reacting to; the rest is context. Wear is NVMe-only and Bad sectors is SATA-only apart from NVMe media errors, so blanks in those columns are expected rather than missing data.

panels.title: Memory against configured limit

targets.expr: 100 * max by (host, name) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{host="$host",name!="",name!~"[0-9a-f]{64}"}) / on(host, name) max by (host, name) (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{host="$host",name!="",name!~"[0-9a-f]{64}"} > 0 < 8e9)

panels.description: Only containers with a deploy.resources.limits.memory below the host total appear here. Above 85% is the band where an OOM kill becomes likely.

panels.title: CPU throttling

targets.expr: 100 * max by (host, name) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{host="$host",name!="",name!~"[0-9a-f]{64}"}[$__rate_interval])) / on(host, name) max by (host, name) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{host="$host",name!="",name!~"[0-9a-f]{64}"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0)

panels.description: Share of scheduling periods in which the container hit its cpus limit. Sustained throttling shows up to users as latency with no error logged anywhere. Names that are 64-char hex ids are filtered out: cAdvisor emitted those briefly while its docker factory was misconfigured, and they are meaningless here.

panels.title: Containers logging errors (1h)
panels.description: Log lines matching error/fatal/panic/exception, case-insensitive, over the last hour. A steady low count is normal for authentik and crowdsec; a sudden jump is the signal worth chasing.

panels.title: Error log lines over time
panels.description: Same filter, plotted so a spike is visible at a glance.

panels.title: Requests by entrypoint
panels.description: https is the LAN entrypoint (:443); https-external is the internet-facing one (:8443). Traffic appearing on https-external that you did not expect is worth investigating.

panels.title: CrowdSec active decisions
panels.description: Bans currently in force. A sharp step up means an active scan or brute-force attempt.

panels.title: Probe status
panels.description: Every endpoint behind Traefik, plus the services on the other host. TLS expiry is not broken out per endpoint: they all present the same DuckDNS wildcard, so one number in the At a glance row covers it.
